newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ growth prospects unaffected by weak GDP - Birch.
newsitem.headline: NZ growth prospects unaffected by weak GDP - Birch.

text.p: New Zealand's Minister of Finance Bill Birch, said on Monday weak March quarter GDP data did not change the economic conditions that were conducive to further growth.
Earlier, Statistics New Zealand said production-based GDP fell 0.5 percent in the March quarter.
Against the March 1996 quarter it was 1.4 percent higher, while the annual average growth was 2.3 percent.
Economists had expected a quarterly fall of 0.09 percent, while the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on Friday forecast a quarterly rise of 0.3 percent.
Birch said the data confirmed the wisdom of the government taking a "balanced approach" to fiscal management in last week's budget, and the need for the announced ongoing economic reforms.
He said economies moved in cycles and that after four years of continuous growth it was not surprising to see some slow-down.
"Despite the overall quarterly slow-down, investment grew by 2.8 percent, indicating businesses are placing themselves to take advantage of imminent higher economic growth," Birch said.

"More importantly, today's GDP figures do not change the economic conditions which are conducive to further growth -- interest rates are down, the exchange rate has weakened, the inflation outlook is good and the world economy is strong."
